Every time he heard a loud bang or explosion, he was thrust back to that place, where he felt powerless. The sounds were not merely auditory triggers; they ignited memories that surged forth, often leaving him in physical pain reminiscent of the horrors he had experienced. Hearing those familiar sounds would transport Ravi back to the scene of the explosions, where he was once again engulfed in chaos, each recollection tightening the grip of his trauma. His emotional instability was compounded by a deep-seated belief that he had violated his own values during the crisis. This conviction fed his sense of threat, leading him to perceive even mundane interactions as potential sources of danger that could reinforce his feelings of alienation.
